resources.string: The stream comes from YouTube, the account is yours. No ads, no analytics, no background event reporting: history and stats stay in a file on this computer — check it against the sources.
Personal finances that never leave your device.
Files are in %1$s: any player opens them, and they copy to other places as they are.
No SAPISID in the cookie: copy the whole Cookie header.
The sign-in window was closed before it finished.
mpv not found — install it (sudo pacman -S mpv)
YouTube didn\'t return audio for this track
Press ? or Esc to close. Media keys on the keyboard work through the system (MPRIS) and aren\'t bound here. Rebind in Settings → Keys.
Esc cancels while waiting for a key.
Or paste the cookie by hand: music.youtube.com → DevTools → Network → the Cookie header of any request.
A browser window opens with the real Google sign-in page. You type the password yourself — the app never sees it and only takes the YouTube cookie.
No Chromium-based browser found (chromium, chrome, brave…). Sign in with a cookie.
The browser didn\'t open the debug port
Waiting for sign-in in the browser window…
Play a track and its lyrics show up here.
The playlist is empty or didn\'t open.
The queue is empty. Play any track.
Type a query and press Enter.
The player shows the visualizer where the cover would be. The key V does the same.

`w0y --do play_pause` sends a command to the running app, so you can bind any action to a key in your desktop (KDE, GNOME, sway). `w0y --do list` prints all commands. Media keys already work through the system (MPRIS).
Library, history and settings live in one file: %1$s
Where the sound goes. “auto” — whatever the system decides.
Where tracks are saved: one file per track, any player opens them. Used now: %1$d MB.
Ten bands through mpv. Changes apply to the playing track right away.
All settings as one JSON — to move them to another computer.
Glass — panels blur what\'s under them. Matte — plain rounded panels, lighter on the GPU.
Click a shortcut to remove it, “+” adds one. A key already used elsewhere moves to the new action. The Russian layout works too.
The full list of shortcuts in one window. The same list opens with ? or F1.
“Original” keeps the file exactly as YouTube serves it. MP3 converts it with ffmpeg at 320 kbps with title, artist and album.
MP3 conversion needs ffmpeg, which isn\'t installed. Files are kept as YouTube serves them.
No folder picker found. Install zenity or kdialog.
A system notification with the title and artist whenever the track changes.
Which stream to ask YouTube for. High is the best available; economical starts faster.
While stand mode is open the system won\'t dim the screen or go to sleep.
Open stand mode now. The B key does the same; Esc closes it.
A dimmed cover behind the bars.
Replaces the cover in the player. The sound is taken from w0y\'s own stream in PipeWire/PulseAudio — no microphone, no delay.
30 saves power, 60 is smoother. It stops completely when the visualizer isn\'t on screen.
The visualizer needs pactl and parec (package pipewire-pulse or pulseaudio-utils). They weren\'t found, so the option is off.
Play a track and similar ones show up here.
Picked from YouTube radio and your taste: who you listen to most, what you liked and searched. What just played goes last.
Pitch is changed by rubberband, reverb by an ffmpeg filter inside mpv.
Play a track: sound is set for each track separately.
Average over the last %1$d starts: %2$d ms.
Shows up after the first play.
Frees the space. Copies you made elsewhere stay.
The app\'s language. “System” follows the computer.
Erases everything in the app: settings, library, history, account sign-in and downloads. Files you copied elsewhere stay.
Time from click to first sound, measured on this computer. %1$s
For a screen mounted upside down. The button in stand mode flips it too.
What is big on the stand screen. Click and hold to switch.
Music from YouTube with no ads and no limits. With your account, your playlists and downloads on your computer.
Quiet and thin: lines instead of shadows, one accent. The default look.
Makes the whole window larger or smaller. Applies at once; 125–150% suits a big monitor.
The window closes, music keeps playing. Bring it back or quit from the tray icon.
Off by default. Turning it on adds an autostart entry for your user only.
Version, system, audio engine, recent events and crash records. No tokens or cookies. The text is copied to the clipboard and sent nowhere.
Checks the connection to YouTube Music and GitHub — the only places the app talks to.
The latest release has no file for this system.
What is inside: libmpv, fonts, libraries. License texts ship next to the app.
One click selects (Ctrl and Shift select several), double-click plays. Off — one click plays at once.
"Auto" picks light animations on a weak computer. "Off" removes transitions entirely.
One file: settings, likes, playlists, history, stats. Your account sign-in is not included. Restoring replaces current data; a copy stays in library.json.bak.
Double-click the disc to pause · drag sideways to change track · press, hold and move around the ring to seek
How big the disc is in the player.
A thin ring around the cover that fills as the track plays.
The cover slowly turns while music plays. Only with full animations.
How dark the cover behind the Poster layout is.
What lies behind the player: a soft glow in the cover colours, the blurred cover, aurora, the app background or plain black.
You can drag files into the window.
File not found — it may have been deleted
Nothing is queued after this. Try the Similar tab.
A big clock next to the title.
Show or hide the side bar
Show or hide the bottom player bar
The menu on the left. A hidden bar comes back with the tab at the left edge or Ctrl+B.
The controls at the bottom of the window. A hidden bar comes back with the tab at the bottom edge or Ctrl+Shift+B. The big player does not need it: all controls sit under the cover.
